# Governance 4.5.7

Local builds can complete and release their reservations using the native supervisor's existing
records. An explicit local-build declaration binds real POSIX lock files; one cleanup owner handles
normal finish, interrupted recovery and historical build recovery. Project wrappers no longer need
a duplicate process-closure report for this route.

New Gradle/build dispatch requires a cleanup declaration before taking reservations. Busy locks,
live processes and changed ownership remain protected. Interrupted release resumes without
rebuilding, changing original results or releasing a successor's claim. Unknown workflows expose
the cleanup blocker instead of silently losing its cause.

This release adds an optional recipe field and an explicit historical recovery selection. Existing
pins/bindings remain unchanged until deliberate adoption. Device and remote cleanup retain their
existing owners. Runtime qualification is synthetic/offline; it is not product or device acceptance.
